Compare a personal game collection with a reference season

Source: R/compare_personal_season.R
compare_personal_season.Rd

Sample same-size game collections without replacement, optionally preserving the personal collection's counts within strata such as home/away or opponent. This is a descriptive reference distribution, not an estimate of the effect of scorekeeping. Games are assumed exchangeable within each supplied stratum.

Usage

compare_personal_season(
  games,
  game_ids,
  metric = "win",
  strata = "home",
  simulations = 2000L
)

Arguments

games

Data frame with unique character game_id, nonmissing team and season, a finite numeric metric, and any requested stratum columns. Must contain exactly one team's one season, including the selected games.

game_ids

Unique character IDs of the personally recorded games.

metric

Name of the numeric game-level measure to average. Default win requires 0/1 values, so the mean is winning percentage.

strata

Character vector of columns to match jointly. Default home preserves home/away counts. Use character(0) for unrestricted sampling.

simulations

Positive integer number of draws; default 2000.

Value

A list containing summary (one row with sample sizes, selected, other-game and season means, selected-minus-other difference, 2.5th and 97.5th reference percentiles, and a tie-adjusted percentile rank), simulated_means, and settings. The reference range is not a confidence interval for a causal effect or underlying player ability. Summary fields include personal_mean, other_mean, season_mean, difference, reference_low, reference_high, and reference_percentile.

Details

Supply complete game-level records, not one row per upload or team side. Duplicates and missing IDs are errors. At least one selected and one unselected game are required. Sampling includes the selected games in the reference population. Use set.seed() before calling for reproducibility. More detailed strata can leave little variation. Unmeasured selection differences remain, and this function does not test many patterns at once.

See also

season_games(), reviewed_team_seasons, calculate_batting_stats(), calculate_run_impact()

Examples

games <- data.frame(game_id = letters[1:8], team = "Demo", season = 2026,
                    home = rep(c(TRUE, FALSE), 4), win = c(1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0))
set.seed(457)
compare_personal_season(games, c("a", "b", "c"), simulations = 100)$summary
#>   metric selected_games other_games personal_mean other_mean season_mean
#> 1    win              3           5     0.6666667        0.4         0.5
#>   difference reference_low reference_high reference_percentile
#> 1  0.2666667     0.3333333              1                 64.5
